dish: Kikunotsuyu awamori (incl. Kikunotsuyu VIP Gold kūsu) distilled with Miyako's hard coral-limestone water
n: Kikunotsuyu Shuzō awamori distillery, Miyako (菊之露酒造)
w: Founded in 1928 in Hirara, Kikunotsuyu is one of Miyako's oldest and best-known awamori distillers, using the island's mineral-rich hard water from its coral-limestone bedrock; its aged awamori features in the Okinawa Regional Taxation Bureau's awamori appraisal.

dish: Tama no Tsuyu awamori and aged kūsu (traditional jikabi direct-fire still)
n: Tamanaha Shuzōsho awamori distillery, Ishigaki (玉那覇酒造所)
w: Billed as Yaeyama's oldest awamori distillery, the family-run Tamanaha makes Tama no Tsuyu, a rare Ishigaki brand seldom found on the mainland; its kūsu appears in the Okinawa Regional Taxation Bureau's awamori appraisal results.

dish: Donan hanazake — 60 % first-run awamori made only on Yonaguni
n: Donan (Kokusen Awamori) hanazake distillery, Yonaguni (どなん 国泉泡盛)
w: Distilling on Yonaguni since 1958, Kokusen makes Donan, including the 60 % hanazake that only Yonaguni's distilleries are licensed to produce — awamori's highest strength, originally a ceremonial spirit. Visitors can see production and buy small bottles at the hilltop plant it moved to in 2011.
